clips.caption: Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the exact moment you've earned the right to say "I am a millionaire" — and why saying it before you believe it just keeps you stuck. Which stage are you on right now?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on why the very first step toward a big goal isn't "I want" — it's a much smaller word. Would you actually say it out loud?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the picture you carry of yourself, and why saying something that doesn't match it creates conflict instead of results. What does your picture say?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on why saying "I want to be a millionaire" can trigger old beliefs that fight back. Which belief about money did you grow up with?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the difference between "I will" (someday) and "I am in the process" (today). What are you doing right now that proves you're in the process?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on why "I am a millionaire" is where you finish, not where you start. Where are you on the ladder right now?

Ad: Kevin Trudeau tells the story of the moment he was finally given what he was told was a miracle that takes only five seconds.

He was sitting at the edge of his seat, expecting something huge. The lesson was a single sentence: take 100 percent responsibility for everything that happens in your life, without exception and without condition.

Then everyone stood, shook his hand, and the lesson was over.

Kevin explains that it's quick to hear and takes years to live.

What would change if you took that sentence seriously?

#mindset #responsibility #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau recalls the classic Earl Nightingale recording, The Strangest Secret: you become what you think about most of the time.

Kevin tells how he laughed when he first heard it, because he was always thinking about girls. Everyone in the room laughed too, but they understood the distinction. You become what you think about and feel about most of the time.

Thoughts are things. So his advice is to control your thoughts and feelings, feel good now, and keep working on being a better you.

What do you think about most of the time?

#mindset #thoughts #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau shares a small story that shows how distance grows between two people.

A man comes home from lunch and tells his wife where he went and what he ate. Every word is true.

What he leaves out is who he had lunch with. He didn't lie, but he wasn't honest either.

Kevin says there is a real difference between telling the truth and being honest. Small omissions can build a quiet barrier between people.

Where have you noticed the gap between the two?

#relationships #communication #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau gives a straight answer on whether there is only one soulmate.

His reasoning is simple. If you think there is exactly one person on the whole planet meant for you, that's a stretch.

He compares it to asking whether any other planets could support life. Just look at the odds.

Kevin says there are likely many people you could connect with deeply, and that changes how you think about finding someone.

Do you believe in the one, or in many?

#soulmate #relationships #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau answers what he would do if he had a roommate who was a slob.

His answer: he wouldn't have that roommate, because he wouldn't be in that situation.

The people around him are honest, kind, loving and good communicators. They don't have buttons that get triggered.

Kevin says that's because of what he is attracting into his life. His view is that the people in your world reflect the person you are.

What does your circle reflect back to you?

#mindset #relationships #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau looks back at a time when nobody carried a credit card.

Back then you had a charge account at the local store, or a charge card from a handful of companies. It was meant for convenience, so you didn't have to carry a lot of cash.

Kevin explains how different that world was from the one we live in now, and why the difference matters.

What do you think changed most between the charge card era and today?

#credit #money #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the key difference between a charge card and a credit card.

With a charge card, the money had to already be in your bank. Sometimes the company even checked with your bank first.

With a credit card, you can spend money you don't have. Kevin explains that a charge card was just a convenience, while a credit card lets you spend beyond what you hold.

It's a simple distinction worth keeping in mind.

When you use a card, do you check the balance in your account first?

#credit #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on a detail about credit scores that many people miss.

Most of us assume that paying by the due date is all that matters. Kevin explains that the card company usually reports your balance to the credit agencies 10 to 15 days before that date.

His advice is to ask your card company when they report, then pay the balance off before that day.

It's a small timing change, and it's the one Kevin calls the magic secret.

Did you know your report date and your due date can be different?

#credit #creditscore #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on a phrase we hear all the time: live within your means.

Kevin says it isn't enough. You have to live below your means.

He points to how his father's generation handled money. They kept housing a small share of income, and they didn't finance cars. They paid cash, and until they could, they went without.

It's an old habit, and Kevin says it's still a strong one.

What's one expense you could trim to live below your means?

#money #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on a rule of thumb for spending.

If you can't pay for something with cash, he says you can't afford it, with the possible exception of a house and a car.

Then he looks at housing itself. Kevin says many people pay too large a share of their income for the home, once you add the mortgage, insurance and upkeep.

He's not a financial planner, and he says so. It's common sense he asks you to apply to your own numbers.

What share of your income goes to housing?

#budget #money #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau paints a picture of what it feels like to be debt free.

Cards at zero, payments current, and some savings set aside for a rainy day.

Kevin says that kind of order brings a feeling of strength and control, and that confidence carries into every other part of your life.

It's less about the numbers and more about the peace of mind they give you.

What would having zero balances change for you?

#debtfree #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau explains what he calls a robust credit file.

His picture is two installment loans, such as a mortgage and a car payment, plus three revolving lines of credit. He says more than that can pull the score down, because it means too much available credit.

He also mentions a home equity line and a line against a stock portfolio. These can sit available without being used.

Which part of your own credit file do you understand least?

#credit #creditscore #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the biggest mistake people make in hard times.

He says it is calling it adversity in the first place. Kevin explains it is simply a situation, and nobody else makes you feel a certain way.

He shares the story of Viktor Frankl, who wrote Man's Search for Meaning while in a concentration camp. Frankl said others could control everything around him, but not his thoughts.

The lesson: you choose what you think, and what you think shapes how you feel.

Where in your life could you choose your thoughts on purpose?

#mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau tells the story of two men on a porch and an old hound dog that keeps moaning but never moves.

When one man asks why the dog won't get up, the other says he's lying on a nail, but it doesn't hurt him enough.

Kevin says people can be the same. They don't like their house, their car or their situation, but the discomfort never gets big enough to force a change.

A change often starts when staying put hurts more than moving.

What is your version of the nail you keep lying on?

#mindset #motivation #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau grew up in a blue collar town and wanted to learn how successful people think.

His plan was simple. He became a caddy at a country club where the members were wealthy, and he watched them closely.

He noticed they talked, thought and carried themselves differently. But they were normal human beings, just like his dad.

The real difference was how they thought and how they saw themselves. That is when he realized he could do it too.

Who are you spending your time around?

#success #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau grew up in a blue collar community where his dad was a welder and his mom stayed home.

Everyone on the street worked a job, hoped to get into the union and dreamed of a government pension.

Kevin learned early that you have to work for yourself and be your own boss.

That lesson sent him to the library to read about people who became very successful.

What did you learn early about work from the people around you?

#entrepreneur #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau tells a story about a friend who taught success seminars but kept stumbling in business.

Every time he looked at a deal he said, "I have a concern." Kevin points out that a concern is fear in words.

His advice was to swap it for "I have a question" or "there's something here we can make better."

The same situation, but now you are the one steering the conversation.

What word do you use out of habit without noticing?

#mindset #communication #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the two most powerful words you use: "I am."

Kevin explains that whatever you put after "I am" is taken by your mind as a statement about your whole being. "I am a loser." "I am a shy person."

Say it often enough and you have spoken it into existence as a fact about yourself. It will not change until you change it with your words first.

It is a short habit to notice, and it can start today.

What do you usually say after "I am"?
